recipes.title: Avocado toast with egg
recipes.description: Two slices of wholegrain toast with mashed avocado and a boiled egg.
steps: Boil the egg for 7 to 9 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Toast the bread and mash the avocado onto it with salt and pepper.
Slice the egg on top and finish with chilli flakes.
recipes.notes: Macros are calculated from typical label values, the same ones the meal plan uses.

recipes.title: Boiled eggs on toast with avocado
recipes.description: Two boiled eggs, a slice of wholegrain toast and a little avocado.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to the boil, lower in the eggs and cook 7 minutes for jammy yolks or 9 to 10 minutes for firm.
Move the eggs to cold water for a minute, then peel.
Toast the bread, mash the avocado on top and season. Serve with the eggs.
recipes.notes: Boil a batch of eggs on Sunday; they keep 5 days in the fridge unpeeled. Macros are calculated from typical label values, the same ones the meal plan uses.

recipes.title: Greek yogurt bowl
recipes.description: Thick Greek yogurt with oats, fruit and a little honey. Five minutes, no cooking.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with the oats and fruit, drizzle with the honey and finish with cinnamon.
recipes.notes: Stir the oats in the night before if you like them soft. Macros are calculated from typical label values, the same ones the meal plan uses.

recipes.title: High-protein breakfast quesadilla
recipes.description: Scrambled egg with cottage cheese, chicken sausage and cheddar, crisped in a tortilla.

ingredients.note: about 18 cm, high-fibre if you can find it

steps: Brown the sausage in a small non-stick pan over medium heat until crisp at the edges, then set aside.
Meanwhile whisk the egg, egg whites, cottage cheese, spring onion, salt and pepper.
Spray the pan and cook the eggs over medium heat, folding as they set, for 2 to 3 minutes until no longer wet.
Heat a clean large pan over medium-low heat, spray it and lay in the tortilla.
Spread half the cheese over one half, top with the egg, sausage and remaining cheese. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until crisp underneath, fold, flip and cook until the cheese melts.
Cut into three and serve.
recipes.notes: The source uses an American low-carb tortilla (very high in fibre), so with a regular wholewheat tortilla expect about 30 kcal more and fewer grams of fibre. Swap the sausage for turkey ham, or leave it out and add peppers or mushrooms. Macros are from the source.

recipes.title: Spinach protein pancakes
recipes.description: Green buckwheat pancakes with buttermilk and a pinch of paprika, good with poached eggs.
steps: Boil the kettle. Put the buttermilk and beaten egg in a food processor.
Put the spinach in a colander and pour boiling water over it to wilt. Squeeze out the water, add to the processor and blitz to a smooth purée.
Mix the flour, baking powder, paprika and salt in a bowl, then gradually stir in the purée. If it is thick, loosen with 1 tbsp water.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat and add 2 or 3 ladles of batter. Cook 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear, flip and cook 1 minute more.
Repeat until you have 12 pancakes. Serve with poached eggs if you like.
recipes.notes: One serving is 3 pancakes. Source macros are for the pancakes only; 2 poached eggs add about 145 kcal and 13 g protein, which makes it a 25 g protein breakfast.

recipes.title: Protein pancakes with banana
recipes.description: Blender pancakes made from eggs, oats, banana and protein powder.
steps: Put the eggs, oats, banana, protein powder, milk, baking powder and cinnamon in a blender and blitz for 1 to 2 minutes until smooth. If the oats have not broken down, blitz for another minute.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a pan and ladle in 2 or 3 rounds of batter with space between them.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the underside is golden, then flip and cook 1 minute more. Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.
Serve with a spoon of Greek yogurt and sliced banana.
recipes.notes: The original also tops them with maple syrup; leave it out or use a little honey. Macros are from the source per serving.

recipes.title: Sweet potato fries with chili cheese
recipes.description: Spiced sweet potato wedges topped with a quick beef chili and melted cheese.

ingredients.note: about 1 kg, halved and cut into wedges, skin on

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Mix the chilli powder and cumin in a small bowl.

Toss the sweet potato wedges with the oil, salt, pepper and half the spice mix. Spread them in one layer in a cast-iron pan or a lined tray and roast for about 35 minutes, until a knife goes in easily.
Meanwhile heat the oil for the topping in a large pan over medium-high heat and soften the onion for a couple of minutes.
Add the mince and break it into fine crumbs. Season with salt, pepper and the rest of the spice mix.
When the beef is cooked, stir in the garlic, then the tomato paste. Sprinkle in the flour, pour in the stock and simmer briefly until slightly thick. Keep warm.
Lower the oven to 180°C. Scatter a third of the cheese over the hot wedges, spoon the chili over and top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake 5 to 10 minutes more until the cheese melts. Finish with spring onion or coriander.

steps.note: Shake the pot every 6 to 7 minutes. They are ready when a knife goes in easily.
Put the topped wedges in a small ovenproof dish that fits on the tray, so the cheese does not drip through.

speedi.note: Adapted from the oven method (200°C, about 35 min). Make the chili topping on the hob, or in the pot on Sear/Sauté (tray removed) while no wedges are cooking.

recipes.notes: Unpeeled, medium sweet potatoes hold their shape best. Ground chicken or turkey works instead of beef. The source lists 510 kcal per serving but no other macros; adding up the ingredients gives about 390, so these macros are my estimate.

recipes.title: Makaronia me kima, Greek spaghetti with mince
recipes.description: Slow-simmered beef mince sauce with brandy, cinnamon, bay and nutmeg over spaghetti with kefalotyri.
steps: Heat the oil in a pot over high heat and brown the mince for 7 to 8 minutes. Stir only now and then so it browns instead of stewing in its juices.
Push the mince to the sides to make a well, add a few drops of oil and the onion, garlic and carrot. Cook 3 to 4 minutes until soft and glossy but not coloured, then stir everything together.
Add the tomato paste, rub it into the base of the pot and cook 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Still on high heat, pour in the brandy and let the alcohol evaporate completely.
Crush the tomatoes by hand or chop them and add them with the stock. When it boils, seal the pot with baking paper and foil under the lid.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 1 hour.
Add salt, pepper, the bay leaves, cinnamon, nutmeg and parsley. Cover again and simmer about 20 minutes more, until the sauce is thick and the mince very tender. Remove the whole spices and parsley.
Boil the spaghetti, drain, return it to the pot and toss with a little olive oil. Serve with the sauce and grated kefalotyri.
recipes.notes: Keep the pot well sealed so the sauce stays rich and does not dry out. The sauce freezes well in portions. Never rinse the pasta in cold water. A full serving is a big plate (about 1,050 kcal); the meal plan uses half. The source gives no macros, so they are estimated, assuming beef mince of about 15% fat and 20 g kefalotyri per plate.

recipes.title: One pot chicken and broccoli pasta
recipes.description: Rigatoni with seared chicken, broccoli, white wine and a cream cheese and sage sauce, finished in one pan.
steps: Heat a deep frying pan over medium heat with the olive oil and brown the chicken on all sides. Add the broccoli and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let the alcohol cook off, then add the pasta and the pasta water and stir for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, add the cream cheese, salt, pepper and sage and stir until the sauce comes together. Serve hot.
recipes.notes: A full serving is a big plate (about 800 kcal); the meal plan uses half. The source gives no macros, so they are estimated, assuming 400 g chicken, full-fat cream cheese and 1 tbsp oil.

recipes.title: Chicken and courgette patties
recipes.description: Juicy chicken patties with grated courgette, mozzarella, parmesan and thyme, baked rather than fried.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and line a tray with baking paper.
Grate the courgettes on the coarse side, salt them and leave for 5 minutes. Squeeze them very well in a clean tea towel and put them in a large bowl.
Add everything else and knead well (gloves help) until evenly mixed.
Shape into patties of 80 to 100 g, about 8, and set them on the tray.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until cooked through. Serve with a salad or roast potatoes.

steps.food: Patties, in one layer (2 batches if they do not fit)
steps.note: Brush the tray with a little oil instead of using baking paper. Turn the patties halfway.

speedi.note: Adapted from the oven method (200°C fan, 20 to 25 min). Chicken must reach 74°C in the middle; check the first batch.

recipes.notes: Chilling the mince for an hour before mixing gives more flavour. One serving is 2 patties. The source gives no macros, so they are estimated from the ingredients.

recipes.title: Air fryer pork chops with potatoes
recipes.description: Mustard, lemon and oregano pork chops with crisp oregano chips, both done in the air fryer.
steps: Cut the potatoes into thin chips, put them in a bowl and toss by hand with the olive oil, salt and oregano.
Score the fat along the edge of the chops in a few places.
Rub the chops on both sides with the lemon juice and salt.
Brush both sides with the olive oil, mustard and oregano.
Double-basket air fryer: put the potatoes in one basket and the chops in the other and cook at 200°C for 30 minutes, turning the chops and tossing the potatoes halfway.
Single-basket air fryer: cook the chops and the potatoes separately, 30 minutes each at 200°C.
Serve with mustard and fresh oregano.
recipes.notes: Tested in an 11 litre, 2400 W double-basket air fryer; smaller models may need a few minutes more.

steps.note: Turn halfway. Pork is done at 63°C in the middle; rest 3 minutes.

speedi.note: The Speedi has one pot, so cook the potatoes and the chops one after the other, as the recipe says for single-basket air fryers. Keep the first batch warm in a low oven. Times are adapted from the recipe’s 30 minutes at 200°C; check the chops from 18 minutes.

recipes.title: Salmon feta pasta with red peppers
recipes.description: Salmon, feta and red peppers baked in one dish, then broken up into a creamy sauce for pasta.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the salmon, pepper strips and the feta block in a large baking dish. Drizzle with the olive oil and season the salmon and peppers lightly; feta is already salty.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until the peppers are soft and catching at the edges and the feta is golden.
Meanwhile cook the pasta in salted boiling water as the packet says. Keep 120 ml of the pasta water before draining.
Take the dish out and break up the feta with a fork into a creamy sauce. Flake the salmon gently.
Stir in the basil, garlic and chilli flakes.
Add the pasta and mix, loosening the sauce with pasta water as needed.
recipes.notes: Adapted: red peppers replace the cherry tomatoes in the original. Peppers release less juice than tomatoes, so you will likely need more of the pasta water. The photo shows the original version with tomatoes. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Macros are the source figures, adjusted for the pepper swap.

recipes.title: Gigantes, baked giant beans
recipes.description: Giant beans baked slowly in a tomato, carrot and celery sauce with parsley and dill.
steps: The night before, soak the beans in plenty of water with a little baking soda dissolved in it. If you know the beans cook easily, or you can soak them for more than 12 hours, skip the soda.
Next day rinse them well, cover with cold water and boil for about 40 minutes until soft, skimming the foam. Drain and spread them in a 37 x 25 cm tray (or a 35 cm round one).
Heat the oven to 200°C, top and bottom heat.
Heat half the olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat and cook the onion for about 10 minutes until translucent.
Add the garlic, celery and carrot and cook 2 to 3 minutes more. They should soften without colouring.
Add the sugar, tomatoes, parsley, salt and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the beans, then add the rest of the olive oil and the water.
Bake for about 45 minutes, until the sauce has reduced and only the oil is left around the beans.
recipes.notes: With a fan oven, use the middle shelf, a lower temperature and cover the tray with foil so the beans do not dry out before they turn creamy. If you need to add water while boiling or baking, add boiling water. Avoid yellowed or cracked beans; they are old and will not soften. The source mentions 330 kcal per serving, but the beans and oil alone add up to more, so these macros are my estimate from the ingredients.

recipes.title: Fakes, Greek lentil soup
recipes.description: Small lentils with leek, carrot and tomato, thickened with olive oil and sharpened with vinegar.
steps: Rinse the lentils, boil them in plenty of water for 5 minutes and drain.
Heat 3 to 4 tablespoons of the olive oil in a pot and soften the onion and leek for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and carrot and stir to coat them in the oil.
Add the tomato paste and rub it into the base of the pot with a wooden spoon so it toasts and releases its aroma.
Add the lentils, grated tomato, bay leaves and enough hot water to cover everything.
Cover and cook on low heat for about 30 minutes, until the lentils are soft and the soup has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper, then slowly stir in the rest of the olive oil over low heat so it thickens.
Sprinkle with the vinegar and a little dried oregano, stir, cover and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Serve with olives, feta and bread.
recipes.notes: Cooking time depends on the lentils; they are ready when the soup thickens. A diced potato or sweet potato makes it richer. The source says 4 to 5 servings; the macros are estimated from the ingredients for 5.

recipes.title: Trahanas soup with feta
recipes.description: Sour trahanas simmered with goat milk and finished with sheep and goat butter, feta and lots of black pepper.

ingredients.note: the kind sold in a jar

ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps: Melt half the butter in a medium pot over medium heat and soften the onion for about 5 minutes.
Add the trahanas and stir until it is coated in butter. Pour in the milk and hot water and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until it comes to a boil.
Lower the heat slightly and cook for about 15 minutes more, until the trahanas is soft and the soup has thickened.
Stir in the rest of the butter, the feta, salt and plenty of black pepper, then take off the heat.
recipes.notes: Cooking time depends on the trahanas (homemade, size, how dry it is), so keep an eye on it the first time. Hard feta keeps some bite, soft feta melts in. Chilli flakes (boukovo) are a good alternative to the pepper. Variation: boil the trahanas with the milk, butter, salt and hot water for 15 minutes. Separately soften the onion in 30 ml olive oil for 4 to 5 minutes, stir in 80 g dry mizithra and add it to the pot. Finish with dried mint or oregano, lemon zest and chilli flakes. The source gives no servings; 4 is my assumption. Macros are estimated from the ingredients.

recipes.title: Kelaidi, beef and pepper bake
recipes.description: A layered tray bake from Tyrnavos: potato, horn peppers, sliced beef, tomato and kefalotyri.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C, top and bottom heat. Oil the base of a 25 x 32 cm tray.
Cover the base with the potato slices and season with salt and pepper.
Cover the potatoes fully with the peppers and season.
Lay the beef over the peppers with no gaps and season.
Arrange the tomatoes on top, season, and cover the whole tray with the cheese.
Bake for 1 hour. After the first 30 minutes cover the tray with foil.
Let it cool slightly before serving.
recipes.notes: Every layer is seasoned, so go lightly with the salt. If it releases a lot of liquid at the end, spoon it off carefully. Macros are estimated from the ingredients, assuming about 2 tbsp olive oil.

recipes.title: Cottage cheese lasagna
recipes.description: A lighter lasagna with lean beef, spinach and a cottage cheese filling in place of bechamel.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Warm the oil in a large pan over medium heat and brown the garlic and onion for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the mince, break it up and cook through, about 5 minutes. Stir in the oregano, Italian seasoning, paprika, chilli, salt and pepper.
Add the pasta sauce and leave to simmer while you make the filling.
Mix the cottage cheese, eggs, parmesan, oregano, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper, then stir in the spinach.
Grease a 23 x 33 cm baking dish and spread a spoonful of meat sauce over the base. Lay 4 lasagna sheets across the short side.

Layer 56 g mozzarella, half the meat sauce and half the filling. Repeat with 4 sheets, 56 g mozzarella, the rest of the meat sauce and the rest of the filling, then finish with the last 112 g mozzarella.
Set the dish on a baking tray, cover with foil without touching the cheese and bake for 50 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until browned and bubbling at the edges. Cut into 12 portions.
recipes.notes: The spinach is optional. With fattier mince, drain the fat so the lasagna does not turn watery. No need to blend the cottage cheese.

recipes.title: Two-ingredient naan
recipes.description: No-yeast flatbreads from self-raising flour and Greek yogurt, cooked in a dry pan.
steps: Mix the flour, salt and yogurt in a large bowl, then bring it together into a ball with your hands.
Dust the worktop and the dough with flour. Flatten the dough into a round, cut it into 8 equal pieces and press each into a naan shape.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook each naan for 3 minutes, flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Brush with melted butter if you like.
recipes.notes: One serving is one naan. The cook time is per naan. It needs self-raising flour and will not work with almond or coconut flour.

recipes.title: Ninja Speedi home fries
recipes.description: Paprika potato cubes steamed then crisped in the Ninja Speedi.
steps: Rinse and dry the potato cubes, then toss them in a bowl with the oil, salt, pepper and paprika.
Pour the water into the Speedi pot and set the crisper tray in the bottom position.
Spread the potatoes on the tray, close the lid and flip the switch to Rapid Cooker.
Select Steam Air Fry (Steam & Crisp on US models) at 220°C for 15 to 17 minutes and press start. It steams for about 4 minutes before it starts crisping.
Tip onto a plate and serve.
recipes.notes: The steam stage works like parboiling, which helps the outside crisp.

steps.fn: Steam Air Fry (Steam & Crisp on US models)
steps.note: It steams for about 4 minutes before crisping starts.

speedi.note: The recipe uses 230°C on the US model. The UK/EU model tops out at 220°C on this function, so add a minute or two if they need more colour.

recipes.title: Kreatosoupa, Greek beef soup
recipes.description: Big pieces of beef simmered with potato, carrot and celery, finished with lemon.
steps: Heat a large pot over high heat with a little olive oil. Sear the beef for about 4 minutes per side until deeply browned, then set it aside in a bowl.
In the same pot add a little more oil and cook the potatoes and carrots over medium heat.
Add the celery sticks and onion and stir until the vegetables caramelise.
Return the beef with the tomato paste, then pour in the wine and let the alcohol cook off.
Add the bay leaves, salt, pepper and stock. Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 1.5 hours.
Stir in the leaf celery and lemon juice and take off the heat. Serve hot with fresh pepper and a drizzle of olive oil.
recipes.notes: Keep the beef in large pieces so it does not fall apart. For rice or orzo in the soup, add it for the last 15 minutes. Kcal, protein and carbs are from the source. Fat and fibre are estimated.

recipes.title: Melitzanosalata, smoky aubergine dip
recipes.description: Charred aubergine and red pepper with garlic, vinegar, parsley and olive oil.

ingredients.item: apple cider vinegar or white wine vinegar
spring onion, parsley and olive oil

steps: Leave the skin on the aubergines and prick them all over with a fork.

On a gas hob: char them directly over a high flame for 20 to 25 minutes, turning, until soft with burnt skin. In the oven: bake at 180°C fan for 30 minutes, then grill at 230°C for 10 minutes, turning often.
Cool for 5 minutes, halve lengthways and scoop the flesh into a clean tea towel. Squeeze hard to remove the bitter juices, then chop the flesh finely and put it in a bowl.
Char the pepper the same way for 10 to 15 minutes until soft. Put it in a bowl, cover and leave for 15 to 20 minutes, then peel, deseed and cut into 1 cm cubes. Add to the aubergine.
Blitz the garlic, vinegar and olive oil in a small chopper and stir into the vegetables with salt and pepper.
Finely chop the spring onion greens and parsley leaves and mix them in. Taste, then serve with a little more spring onion, parsley and olive oil on top.
recipes.notes: Charring over gas gives the smoky flavour. It tastes better after resting for a while.

recipes.title: Beef giouvetsi
recipes.description: Slow-baked beef in a cinnamon and clove tomato sauce, finished with orzo in the same pot.

ingredients.note: plus 250 ml very hot water for the orzo

steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan.
Toss the beef in a bowl with about half the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Brown the beef in batches in a deep pan over high heat, then move it to a lidded casserole.
Lower the heat to medium. In the same pan cook the onion and celery in the remaining 2 to 3 tablespoons of oil, scraping the base, until caramelised.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine, then tip everything into the casserole.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, chopped tomatoes, water and bay leaves. Cover and bake for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the beef is tender.
Take the casserole out, stir in the orzo with 250 ml of very hot water and return to the oven for 20 minutes, stirring often.
Check the salt and pepper and serve with grated kefalotyri.
recipes.notes: If the orzo soaks up the liquid quickly, add a little more hot water. Kcal, protein and carbs are from the source. Fat and fibre are estimated.
